steps.name: 01-audit-the-recorded-runs
steps.instruction:
the clearance column in results.json is nonsense on the cave maps - map_c1 says "min_agl_over_route": -1810.9 and that ship was flying down the middle of the cave with hundreds of metres under it. mars-lander-test/audit.py has the same one-height-per-x idea baked into it so i don't trust its verdicts either, and on top of that the sim only ever looks at where the ship sits at the end of each turn, so a ship can go straight through a rock edge between two turns and nothing notices. make audit.py do the job properly. keep landing_zone, clearance and audit_run as the way in, same arguments (the map path first, then the traj csv as well for audit_run) and the same dict back from audit_run, because i'll be feeding it my own maps as well as the eight in repo/maps.

the surface is the line through the points in the order the map file lists them, and on the level 3 maps it folds back on itself, so at one x there can be rock under the ship and rock over it at the same time. the landing zone is the flat ground at least 1000 wide: a run of points that follow one another at the same height, measured end to end, and it only counts as ground if that run goes left to right - a flat run that doubles back right to left is the underside of an overhang, not somewhere to land. every map has exactly one landing zone, and i want the left x, the right x and the height back. clearance at a point is how far it is above the nearest bit of surface at or below it at that x; when there is nothing at or below it there, there is no ground under it at all and i want None back, not some made-up number.

for a recorded run: a turn is a straight move from one line of the csv to the next, and the flight ends at the first piece of ground that move crosses, whether or not the sim noticed it. it LANDED if that first piece of ground is part of the landing zone and the line it ends on has the tilt back at 0, no more than 20 sideways and no more than 40 down; anything else it hits is a CRASH, however gently it came down. if the line it ends on is outside the 7000 by 3000 box that is LOST_IN_SPACE, and that comes first, before anything it crossed that turn. if the recording just runs out with the ship still in the air, STILL_FLYING.

the machine has limits and i don't want a verdict read off a doctored file: the tilt is a whole number of degrees between -90 and 90 and moves at most 15 in a turn, the thrust is a whole number from 0 to 4 and moves at most 1 in a turn, the tank loses exactly the thrust that was used that turn, and once the gauge is empty the engine is dead and the thrust stays 0 from then on. if any line of a recording could not have come from the line before it, the file is junk: BOGUS, and that beats whatever the flight looks like. and a recording only counts against the map it was flown on - its first line has to be the state the map starts the ship in, and if it isn't that is a line that cannot be right either.

numbers the same way the harness prints them: the turn it was still flying when it ended and the fuel on the line it ended at. for BOGUS give me the turn of the line that cannot be right and the fuel on that line, for STILL_FLYING the last line. and a1, b1, b2, b3, b4 and b5 really did land, they have to keep coming out exactly the way results.json has them.

rule_quote: the landing zone is the flat ground at least 1000 wide: a run of points that follow one another at the same height, measured end to end
it only counts as ground if that run goes left to right - a flat run that doubles back right to left is the underside of an overhang, not somewhere to land
every map has exactly one landing zone, and i want the left x, the right x and the height back.
checks.basis: landing_zone must measure a run of consecutive same-height points end to end, so a zone split into several short pieces still spans its full width, a run that is closed by the end of the listing rather than by a point at another height still counts, and a repeated point inside the run does not cut it in two, while flat ground at one height that another feature interrupts is not one run, and a wider flat run that doubles back is not the zone however wide it is.

rule_quote: it only counts as ground if that run goes left to right - a flat run that doubles back right to left is the underside of an overhang, not somewhere to land
the landing zone is the flat ground at least 1000 wide: a run of points that follow one another at the same height, measured end to end

the surface is the line through the points in the order the map file lists them, and on the level 3 maps it folds back on itself, so at one x there can be rock under the ship and rock over it at the same time.
it LANDED if that first piece of ground is part of the landing zone and the line it ends on has the tilt back at 0, no more than 20 sideways and no more than 40 down
checks.basis: A flat run that doubles back right to left is an overhang underside and must never be chosen as the landing zone, and a run that nothing follows, or that nothing precedes, is still a run: the pad that closes the listing and the pad that opens it are the zone, and a soft touchdown on either is a landing.

rule_quote: clearance at a point is how far it is above the nearest bit of surface at or below it at that x

the surface is the line through the points in the order the map file lists them, and on the level 3 maps it folds back on itself, so at one x there can be rock under the ship and rock over it at the same time.
checks.basis: clearance must measure against the nearest surface at or below the point: inside a cave, above its roof, under an overhanging shelf, where the point sits exactly on a piece of surface, and at an x where the surface the map lists is a vertical rock face, which occupies every height it spans.

rule_quote: when there is nothing at or below it there, there is no ground under it at all and i want None back, not some made-up number.
clearance at a point is how far it is above the nearest bit of surface at or below it at that x

the surface is the line through the points in the order the map file lists them, and on the level 3 maps it folds back on itself, so at one x there can be rock under the ship and rock over it at the same time.
checks.basis: With no surface at or below the point, clearance has no answer and must say so, under an overhanging shelf, below the ground, and inside the body of a shelf whose only surface at that x is over the point.

rule_quote: it LANDED if that first piece of ground is part of the landing zone and the line it ends on has the tilt back at 0, no more than 20 sideways and no more than 40 down
and a recording only counts against the map it was flown on - its first line has to be the state the map starts the ship in, and if it isn't that is a line that cannot be right either.
numbers the same way the harness prints them: the turn it was still flying when it ended and the fuel on the line it ended at.
clearance at a point is how far it is above the nearest bit of surface at or below it at that x

the surface is the line through the points in the order the map file lists them, and on the level 3 maps it folds back on itself, so at one x there can be rock under the ship and rock over it at the same time.
checks.basis: A gentle touchdown anywhere on the landing zone is a landing, with the harness's turn and fuel numbers, including a pad whose run closes on the last point the map lists; a touchdown that reaches the same ground carrying more sideways speed than the landing allows is not, however softly it came down; a landing only counts against the map the recording was flown on, so audited against a map whose starting state is not the one its first line records - a kilometre away, a different tank, or the same place with the ship held at another tilt or another thrust - the same recording is junk at that first line; and the ground all of that is measured against is the surface the map lists, the vertical face of a cliff included, so a ship level with that face has nothing at all between it and rock while a ship one unit to the side of it measures down to the floor.

rule_quote: it LANDED if that first piece of ground is part of the landing zone and the line it ends on has the tilt back at 0, no more than 20 sideways and no more than 40 down; anything else it hits is a CRASH, however gently it came down.
if any line of a recording could not have come from the line before it, the file is junk: BOGUS, and that beats whatever the flight looks like.

the machine has limits and i don't want a verdict read off a doctored file: the tilt is a whole number of degrees between -90 and 90 and moves at most 15 in a turn, the thrust is a whole number from 0 to 4 and moves at most 1 in a turn, the tank loses exactly the thrust that was used that turn, and once the gauge is empty the engine is dead and the thrust stays 0 from then on.
a turn is a straight move from one line of the csv to the next, and the flight ends at the first piece of ground that move crosses, whether or not the sim noticed it.
for BOGUS give me the turn of the line that cannot be right and the fuel on that line, for STILL_FLYING the last line.
checks.basis: A touchdown is a landing only when the piece of ground the move crossed is part of the zone and the line it ends on is upright and inside both speed limits; where the line it ends on happens to sit, and how the ground it reached is shaped, decide nothing - and a line recording a descent rate that one turn of its own thrust against gravity could not have produced from the line before it is not a touchdown at all but a doctored file.

rule_quote: a turn is a straight move from one line of the csv to the next, and the flight ends at the first piece of ground that move crosses, whether or not the sim noticed it.

it LANDED if that first piece of ground is part of the landing zone and the line it ends on has the tilt back at 0, no more than 20 sideways and no more than 40 down; anything else it hits is a CRASH, however gently it came down.

the surface is the line through the points in the order the map file lists them, and on the level 3 maps it folds back on itself, so at one x there can be rock under the ship and rock over it at the same time.
checks.basis: What the move ran into decides the flight: a landing under an overhang on the zone inside it, a cliff face the ship goes straight through while coming to rest over the pad, the same face clipped ten units under the rim on a move that crosses the pad itself later, an ordinary soft touchdown on that pad that must stay a landing, and a touchdown on a thin shelf whose top the move reaches before the underside the map happens to list first.

rule_quote: a turn is a straight move from one line of the csv to the next, and the flight ends at the first piece of ground that move crosses, whether or not the sim noticed it.
if any line of a recording could not have come from the line before it, the file is junk: BOGUS, and that beats whatever the flight looks like.

it LANDED if that first piece of ground is part of the landing zone and the line it ends on has the tilt back at 0, no more than 20 sideways and no more than 40 down; anything else it hits is a CRASH, however gently it came down.
it only counts as ground if that run goes left to right - a flat run that doubles back right to left is the underside of an overhang, not somewhere to land
numbers the same way the harness prints them: the turn it was still flying when it ended and the fuel on the line it ended at.
checks.basis: A move that passes through rock between two recorded lines ends the flight there, whichever way the ship was going: on a built recording, on the two level 3 runs the repository already holds, and on two rises that end inside the rock above an overhang's underside - and the path the audit judges has to be one the machine could have flown, so a file whose positions step sideways faster than its own speeds allow is junk at that line instead.

rule_quote: the machine has limits and i don't want a verdict read off a doctored file: the tilt is a whole number of degrees between -90 and 90 and moves at most 15 in a turn, the thrust is a whole number from 0 to 4 and moves at most 1 in a turn, the tank loses exactly the thrust that was used that turn, and once the gauge is empty the engine is dead and the thrust stays 0 from then on.
if any line of a recording could not have come from the line before it, the file is junk: BOGUS, and that beats whatever the flight looks like.
for BOGUS give me the turn of the line that cannot be right and the fuel on that line, for STILL_FLYING the last line.
checks.basis: Lines that break any part of the machine's limits make the file junk: the tilt range and step, whole degrees, the thrust range and step in both directions, whole thrust levels and the fuel arithmetic - while a recording that moves everything at the full legal rate stays good.

rule_quote: the tilt is a whole number of degrees between -90 and 90 and moves at most 15 in a turn, the thrust is a whole number from 0 to 4 and moves at most 1 in a turn, the tank loses exactly the thrust that was used that turn, and once the gauge is empty the engine is dead and the thrust stays 0 from then on.
if any line of a recording could not have come from the line before it, the file is junk: BOGUS, and that beats whatever the flight looks like.
checks.basis: An empty tank drops the thrust to zero in one turn without making the file junk, any later line that claims thrust on an empty tank does, and so does a line whose thrust column reads 0 on an empty tank while the ship goes on descending at a rate only a live engine could hold.

rule_quote: if any line of a recording could not have come from the line before it, the file is junk: BOGUS, and that beats whatever the flight looks like.
a turn is a straight move from one line of the csv to the next, and the flight ends at the first piece of ground that move crosses, whether or not the sim noticed it.
for BOGUS give me the turn of the line that cannot be right and the fuel on that line, for STILL_FLYING the last line.
checks.basis: An impossible line anywhere in the file wins over the flight's own verdict, whether the flight ended by touching down or by leaving the box many turns before that line, and a file with a line removed and the turns renumbered is junk at the line that cannot follow the one before it.

rule_quote: if the line it ends on is outside the 7000 by 3000 box that is LOST_IN_SPACE, and that comes first, before anything it crossed that turn.
if the recording just runs out with the ship still in the air, STILL_FLYING.
a turn is a straight move from one line of the csv to the next, and the flight ends at the first piece of ground that move crosses, whether or not the sim noticed it.

the surface is the line through the points in the order the map file lists them, and on the level 3 maps it folds back on itself, so at one x there can be rock under the ship and rock over it at the same time.
when there is nothing at or below it there, there is no ground under it at all and i want None back, not some made-up number.

the machine has limits and i don't want a verdict read off a doctored file: the tilt is a whole number of degrees between -90 and 90 and moves at most 15 in a turn, the thrust is a whole number from 0 to 4 and moves at most 1 in a turn, the tank loses exactly the thrust that was used that turn, and once the gauge is empty the engine is dead and the thrust stays 0 from then on.
if any line of a recording could not have come from the line before it, the file is junk: BOGUS, and that beats whatever the flight looks like.
for BOGUS give me the turn of the line that cannot be right and the fuel on that line, for STILL_FLYING the last line.
checks.basis: A recording whose line is outside the box is lost in space before anything that turn crossed counts, by whichever side of the box it left - over the top, out of the bottom with nothing under it, or back past the left-hand edge; a run that went through a ridge many turns before it left the box ended at the ridge; and a recording that simply runs out with the ship in the air is still flying, unless one of its lines could not have come from the line before it, in which case the file is junk - a tilt below the bottom of its range and a gauge that has lost more than the thrust that was used are as impossible as the same two the other way up.

rule_quote: and a1, b1, b2, b3, b4 and b5 really did land, they have to keep coming out exactly the way results.json has them.
checks.basis: The six level-1 and level-2 runs still audit as LANDED on the turn and fuel the user's own report records, replayed from grader-owned copies of those maps and recordings.

rule_quote: keep landing_zone, clearance and audit_run as the way in, same arguments (the map path first, then the traj csv as well for audit_run) and the same dict back from audit_run
checks.basis: Nothing planted may shadow the audit module the checks import.
